text:
jamie: Heads-up — ran into a token propagation edge case when routing v2 requests through api-proxy. If a client sends a user Bearer token + SDK X-Client-Version we currently forward both. That causes downstream services to treat requests as user-authenticated in some DAGs. Need decisions: strip user tokens at gateway, or make SDK opt-in to forward?

riley: Can you paste the proxy snippet so infra can see what we currently send/strip? also curious if this only affects v2 endpoints or v1 too. :eyes:

jamie: current nginx snippet we use in staging (simplified):
```nginx
proxy_set_header Authorization $http_authorization;
proxy_set_header X-Client-Version $http_x_client_version;
proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for;
proxy_pass http://api-backend;
```
No rewrite; so auth header flows through unchanged. This surfaced when the chat service honored user scope even though request came via a server-side SDK key.

neha: SDK note: by design browser SDKs never forward user tokens. Server SDKs had an escape hatch `preserve_user_token` that some older integrators flipped on. For the v2 rollout we can: 1) default to strip user Bearer at gateway, 2) keep gateway passthrough but require explicit opt-in flag in SDK and document it, or 3) add header normalization (e.g., move user token to `x-forwarded-user` so downstream can opt-in). My preference is option 1 for safety.

matt: security + product perspective: option 1 reduces blast radius. But it breaks a small set of customers who relied on passthrough for user impersonation flows. We should identify owners and create migration checklist for them.

tara: SRE: if we change behavior at gateway we need a canary and smoke tests that cover both token-present and token-stripped flows. I can add a smoke case that does: `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer user-test" -H "Authorization-Type: sdk-key" \` but we should instead test using separate headers in scripts.

deploy-bot: Canary deploy started for api-v2-proxy: build-589 :rocket:

riley: Owners: can we nominate migration owners? I'd suggest eng-infra: jamie, sdk: neha, eng: matt, plus outreach: product@. I'll open a migration-owners doc/PR. Also need SDK changelog entry and examples.

jamie: added a short note in the migration-owners doc: https://go/redwood/migration-owners (placeholder) — flagged customers who may be impacted.

neha: I'll draft SDK changelog and add a `preserve_user_token` opt-in flag defaulting to false. Example snippet for server SDK:
```js
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY, preserveUserToken: false });
// set true only for explicit customer use-cases
```
I'll also add a migration note under v2 -> deprecation section.

matt: quick router patch idea (pseudo):
```js
if (!config.preserve_user_token) { delete req.headers['authorization']; }
// or move to x-forwarded-user: req.headers['x-forwarded-user'] = auth;
```
PR incoming after neha's changelog so we coordinate.

tara: staging smoke run results: initial smoke failed for header-copy case, re-ran after small patch and it passed :white_check_mark:. Will run another canary smoke after infra change.

riley: Cool. Action items: jamie -> open infra PR to default-strip and add header normalization, neha -> SDK changelog + opt-in flag PR, matt -> router patch PR, tara -> add smoke tests to canary checklist. I'll schedule a 15m sync if any blockers; otherwise target canary tomorrow 09:30 PT.

jamie: pinging @neha and @matt for code-review pings when PRs are ready. :thumbsup:

neha: will send PR today EOD, ping me for review.

matt: will send router PR after neha; timeline looks good.

riley: Thanks all — keeping this thread for async updates. If someone hits a customer blocker post-change, escalate to #customer-success and tag me.
